facts.text: Marshalltown was named in 1853 by Henry Anson after his former home in Marshall, Michigan.
Henry Anson, settler, described the spot as “the prettiest place in Iowa” and built a log cabin on hill between the Iowa River and Linn Creek in 1851.
In 1862 the Cedar Rapids and Missouri River Railroad reached Marshalltown, sparking rapid growth and later becoming part of the Chicago and North Western Railway.
Marshalltown’s courthouse spire was toppled during a tornado emergency in 2023, a rare event that highlighted the town’s vulnerability to severe weather.
The city hosts the Iowa Veterans Home and Marshalltown Community College, making it a regional hub for veterans and higher education.
